summary:
Assam stands under India's national framework. No Assam-specific statute on legal gender recognition, criminal law or facilities was identified in the sources reviewed, so the national assessment applies to this state.

Complaint machinery under the national Transgender Persons Act has been reachable in Assam. Of the seven cases registered nationally under the Act in 2021, two were registered in Assam; the 2023 national tally recorded none in the state. A Queerbeat crime-data report of 30 January 2026 cautions that these national counts are themselves very small, 20 cases across 2019 to 2023, because police-registration bias suppresses recording. A low Assam count therefore does not indicate low incidence, and the year-to-year swing between two cases and none is a movement within numbers too small to rank years against each other.

A 2025 survey cited in the same report found that 27.2% of transgender respondents reported physical violence and 22.3% reported sexual violence. The sources supply no general-population rate for the same period, so the figures establish exposure within the surveyed transgender population rather than a measured excess over background violence.

State-level welfare machinery was absent. A December 2021 reply to Parliament listed the 12 states and union territories that had constituted Transgender Welfare Boards under the 2019 Rules, and Assam was not among them, meaning no state welfare board existed there as of that date. No later status for Assam is sourced.
tangentialFactors:
Assam accounted for two of the seven Transgender Persons Act cases registered nationally in 2021, a substantial share of a national total that the Queerbeat report of 30 January 2026 describes as too small to support comparisons between states. The report attributes the small totals to police-registration bias rather than to an absence of violence, which applies to Assam's rows as it does to every other state's.

Assam's non-inclusion in the December 2021 parliamentary reply places it outside the group of 12 states and union territories that had set up Transgender Welfare Boards by then. The sources document no equivalent Assam body and no later assessment of whether one was created.
localsOnly:
Residents of Assam seeking redress for offences under the Transgender Persons Act have filed complaints that reached registration: two of the seven cases registered nationally in 2021 were Assam cases, and the 2023 national tally recorded none in the state.

Residents had no state Transgender Welfare Board to approach as of December 2021, when a reply to Parliament listed the 12 states and union territories that had constituted such boards and Assam was not among them. Welfare and grievance channels for transgender residents therefore ran through the national framework alone at that date.

Violence exposure recorded among transgender respondents in the 2025 survey stood at 27.2% for physical violence and 22.3% for sexual violence, against a national registration record of 20 Transgender Persons Act cases across 2019 to 2023. The gap between the two is the report's central finding: reporting barriers, not low incidence, shape the official counts.
outOfScopeNotes:
No Assam-specific judicial decisions, police-practice documentation, detention accounts, facilities rules or transition-related healthcare access data were found in the sources reviewed; the state-level picture rests on complaint-registration counts and the welfare-board list alone.

The status of a Transgender Welfare Board in Assam after December 2021 is unresolved. The sources establish the position at that date and record no later development either way.

The 2025 survey figures of 27.2% physical and 22.3% sexual violence are reported without a general-population comparison rate for the same period, so no measured excess over background violence can be stated. Sampling details beyond the respondent group and the year are not specified in the inventory.

Whether the police-registration bias the Queerbeat report of 30 January 2026 documents operates with particular intensity in Assam is not sourced; the report's caution is stated at national level.
